To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
technology is a powerful tool for anti-trafficking advocates and that it has been used to help them fight trafficking.

1) The trafficking-technology nexus has emerged as a new site of governance, 2) The trafficking-technologies nexus has been constructed as a tri-partite response, 3) This tri-partite response is animated by a law-and-order agenda, 4) It is operationalized through augmented surveillance, 5) It is maintained by the integration of technology expertise and advocates, and 6) It has purchase for students in gender and sexuality studies, and neoliberal governmentity

the trafficking-technology discourse and practices are a product of a neoliberal governmentality that seeks to manage the problem of trafficking and its associated social and moral risks through surveillance, exclusion, expertise, and the integration of private actors into public anti-trafficking responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how technology has come to be central to the production and maintenance of the contemporary anti-trafficking industry and how this has shaped the contours of anti-trafficking activism and policy.

how technology is implicated in the production of new forms of anti-trafficking governance, the role of the state and its partners in this governance, and the consequences of this governance for the lives of people who are trafficked.
the ways in which anti-trafficking actors are using technology as a tool to identify, locate, and control trafficking victims.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Trafficking-Technology nexus creates new methods of surveillance and exclusion, and that the nexus also creates new methods of expertise.
the Trafficking-Technology nexus is a complex and dynamic system, which has been shaped by various social, economic, and political factors.
technology has been a major facilitator of the trafficking industry, as well as a major disruptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are examining the role of technology in the anti-trafficking movement and the ways in which technology is shaping the movement.
we argue that technology has become a central organizing force in anti-trafficking work, and that this has important consequences for gender, sexuality, race, and class.
the trafficking-technology complex is not only a site of new and emerging forms of power but also a site of new forms of resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technology is not simply a tool to facilitate or disrupt human trafficking but is also a key component in the production of anti-trafficking knowledge and practices.

the trafficking-technology discourse and its accompanying practices of anti-trafficking collaboration are not simply about the role of technology in facilitating and disrupting sex trafficking, but also about how the trafficking-technology response has reconfigured the relationship between state and non-state actors, and the relationship between the state, the market, and civil society.
the trafficking-technology discourse has the potential to reframe the terms and conditions of anti-trafficking work in ways that may be detrimental to the very people the movement claims to protect.
